report.source_text: Light microscopy showed moderate to severe diffuse proliferation of mesangial cells and stroma. The periodic acid-Schiff staining showed moderate to diffuse proliferation of mesangial cells and stroma ( Figure 1A ), and the periodic acid silver methenamine staining and Masson’s staining showed severe diffuse proliferation of mesangial cells and stroma ( Figure 1B ). It was accompanied by diffuse thickening of the basement membrane, small eosinophilic deposits in the subendothelial segment, and microangioma-like expansion of segmental capillary loops. There were vacuoles and granular degeneration of renal tubular epithelial cells, focal atrophy, and a few protein casts were observed in the lumen. Renal interstitial focal lymphocyte and monocyte infiltration with fibrosis, wall thickening of small arteries, intimal fibrosis and sclerosis, and lumen stenosis were also observed.

The renal interstitium was infiltrated by a small number of lymphoid mononuclear cells with collagen fiber proliferation.

clinician.final_diagnosis: mild to moderate mesangial proliferative IgAN (Type IIa)
clinician.trajectory_summary: Mr. Niu, a 70-year-old male with a history of diabetes and hypertension, presented with intermittent facial and bilateral lower extremity edema and increased nocturia. Initial workup revealed nephrotic range proteinuria (5.54 g/24h), microscopic hematuria (RBC 0.61/Hp), hypoalbuminemia (30 g/L), and hyperlipidemia, with preserved renal function (creatinine 57 μmol/L). A kidney biopsy was performed, which showed IgA and C3 deposition on immunofluorescence. Light microscopy revealed moderate to severe diffuse proliferation of mesangial cells and stroma, diffuse thickening of the basement membrane, and small eosinophilic deposits. Electron microscopy confirmed mild to moderate proliferation of glomerular mesangial cells and occasional small electron-dense deposits in the mesangial region. These findings were consistent with mild to moderate mesangial proliferative IgAN (Type IIa).

key_supporting_evidence.claim: Patient presented with intermittent facial and bilateral lower extremity edema and increased nocturia.
Patient had a 26-year history of diabetes mellitus, 20-year history of hypertension, and 20-year history of coronary heart disease.
Urinalysis showed nephrotic range proteinuria (5.54 g/24h) and microscopic hematuria (occult blood, RBC 0.61/Hp).
Blood tests revealed hypoalbuminemia (30 g/L) and hyperlipidemia (total cholesterol 5.60 mmol/L, triglycerides 2.13 mmol/L) with preserved renal function (BUN 7.63 mmol/L, creatinine 57 μmol/L).
Kidney biopsy immunofluorescence showed IgA+ and C3+ deposition.
Kidney biopsy light microscopy showed moderate to severe diffuse proliferation of mesangial cells and stroma, diffuse thickening of the basement membrane, and small eosinophilic deposits.
Kidney biopsy electron microscopy showed mild to moderate proliferation of glomerular mesangial cells and occasional small electron-dense deposits in the mesangial region.
The overall biopsy findings were consistent with mild to moderate mesangial proliferative IgAN (Type IIa).
